items.title: Insight's Obstacle Opens: The Conceit of Birth, Wealth, and Learning

items.zh: 云何毘鉢舍那障？謂樂自恃舉及以掉亂。樂自恃舉者，謂如有一，作是思惟：我生高族，淨信出家，非為下劣，諸餘比丘，則不如是。由此因緣，自高自舉，陵蔑於他。如是我生富族，淨信出家，非為貧匱，我具妙色，喜見端嚴，多聞、聞持、其聞積集，善巧言詞，語具圓滿，諸餘比丘則不如是。由此因緣，自高自舉，陵蔑於他。彼由如是自高舉故，諸有比丘耆年多智、積修梵行，不能時時恭敬請問。彼諸比丘亦不時時為其開發未開發處，為其顯了未顯了處，亦不為其殷到精懇、以慧通達甚深句義方便開示，乃至令其智見清淨。如是名為樂自恃舉毘鉢舍那障。
items.en: What is the obstacle to insight? It is delighting in self-conceit, and restlessness. … It is like one who thinks: I was born into a noble family, and went forth with genuine faith — not of inferior [birth], unlike other monks. … Likewise: I was born into a wealthy family … I possess a fine appearance … I am learned, retentive, my learning accumulated, skilful in speech, complete in expression — unlike other monks. Through this cause, one exalts oneself and looks down on others. … Because of this self-exaltation, one is unable to approach elder monks of great learning and long-cultivated purity with respect and questions from time to time. And those elder monks, in turn, do not, from time to time, open up for such a one what remains unopened … This is called delighting in self-conceit, the obstacle to insight.

items.title: Complacency and Restlessness Complete Insight's Obstacle

items.zh: 又如有一，唯得少分下劣智見安隱而住。彼由如是少分下劣智見安住便自高舉；自高舉故，便生喜足，更不上求。是名樂自恃舉所住毘鉢舍那障。言掉亂者：謂如有一，根不寂靜，諸根掉亂，諸根囂舉。於一切時，惡思所思、惡說所說、惡作所作。不能安住思惟諸法，不能堅固思惟諸法。由此因緣，毘鉢舍那不能圓滿、不得清淨。是名掉亂毘鉢舍那障。
items.en: Furthermore, it is like one who has attained only a small, inferior degree of knowledge and insight, and rests content in it. Resting in such a small, inferior attainment, one becomes conceited; and being conceited, one becomes complacent, seeking nothing higher. This is called the obstacle to insight caused by self-conceit. … Restlessness means being like one whose faculties are unsettled — agitated, unstable. At all times, one's thoughts, speech, and actions are unwholesome. One is unable to reflect on phenomena with any stability, unable to reflect on them with any firmness. Through this cause, insight cannot become complete, cannot become pure. This is called restlessness, the obstacle to insight.

items.title: Section: Freedom From Obstruction Closes in Full

items.zh: 如是二法障奢摩他，謂多放逸，及住非處；二法能障毘鉢舍那，謂樂自恃舉及以掉亂。如是若奢摩他障、若毘鉢舍那障，總名寂靜障。如是名為障之略義。即此略義及前廣辨，總略為一，說名為障。此障相違，當知無障。謂即此障無性、遠離、不合、不會，說名無障。
items.en: Thus two factors obstruct calming: heedlessness, and dwelling in an unsuitable place. And two factors obstruct insight: self-conceit, and restlessness. Both the obstacle to calming and the obstacle to insight are together called the obstacle to stillness. … This brief summary, together with the detailed exposition given before, taken together as one, is called obstruction. Its opposite should be understood as freedom from obstruction — namely, that this obstruction is without any nature of its own, kept far away, not joined [with the mind, as the obstacles to calming], and not encountered [as the obstacles to insight]: this is called freedom from obstruction.

items.title: Section: Generosity Opens — Giving That Serves the Path Itself

items.zh: 云何惠捨？謂若布施，其性無罪，為莊嚴心、為助伴心、為資瑜伽、為得上義而修布施。是名惠捨。
items.en: What is generosity? It means that giving whose nature is blameless — undertaken to adorn the mind, to support the mind, to provide the resources for yogic practice, and to attain the highest good — is called generosity.

items.zh: 問：誰能施？誰所施？用何施？何相施？云何施？何故施？由此因緣，施性無罪。答：

items.title: Who Gives, and the First Recipients: Those in Genuine Hardship

items.zh: 誰能施者，謂施者、施主，是名能施。云何施者？云何施主？謂若自手施，名為施者；若自物施、若欣樂施、非不樂施，名為施主。誰所施者，謂四種所施。一、有苦者，二、有恩者，三、親愛者，四、尊勝者。云何有苦者？謂貧窮者、或乞匃者、或行路者、或悕求者、或盲瞽者、或聾騃者、或無依者、或無趣者、匱乏種種資生具者。復有所餘如是等類，名有苦者。
items.en: Who is able to give? The giver and the donor — these are called the able givers. What is a giver? What is a donor? Giving with one's own hand is called being a giver. Giving one's own property, willingly and not reluctantly, is called being a donor. To whom does one give? There are four kinds of recipients. First, those in hardship … the poor, beggars, travellers, seekers, the blind, the deaf or dull-witted, those without support, those without refuge, and those lacking the various necessities of life. And there are others of this same kind — these are called those in hardship.

items.title: Two More Recipients: Those Who Showed Kindness, and Those Held Dear

items.zh: 云何有恩者？謂或父母、或乳飲者、或養育者、或成長者、或於曠野沙磧等中能濟度者、或飢儉時能賑恤者、或怖怨敵而救援者、或被執縛而能解者、或遭疾病而救療者、教利益者、教安樂者、引利益者、引安樂者、隨所生起諸事務中為助伴者、同歡喜者、同憂愁者、遭厄難時不相棄者。復有所餘如是等類，名有恩者。云何親愛者？謂諸親友，或於其處有愛有敬、或信順語、或數語言談論交往、或有親昵。
items.en: Second, those who have shown kindness: parents; those who nursed one as an infant; those who raised one; those who helped one grow to maturity; those who rescued one in a wilderness or desert; those who gave relief during famine; those who saved one from a feared enemy; those who freed one from captivity; those who healed one during illness; those who taught what brings benefit or ease; those who increased one's benefit or ease; those who assisted in whatever task arose; those who shared one's joy or one's sorrow; and those who did not abandon one in genuine crisis. Third, those held dear: relatives and friends — those towards whom one feels affection and respect, whose words one trusts and follows, with whom one converses often, or with whom one shares real intimacy.

items.zh: 復有所餘如是等類，說名親愛。

items.title: Section: The Venerable, and a Digression on What Truly Determines Merit

items.zh: 云何尊勝？謂若沙門、若婆羅門，世間同許為賢善者、離損害者、極離害者、離貪欲者、為調伏貪而修行者、離瞋恚者、為調伏瞋而修行者、離愚癡者、為調伏癡而修行者。復有所餘如是等類，名尊勝者。
items.en: What is meant by the venerable? Renunciants or brahmins universally acknowledged by the world as genuinely virtuous — free of harm, utterly free of harm; free of desire, or practising to overcome desire; free of aversion, or practising to overcome aversion; free of delusion, or practising to overcome delusion. And there are others of this same kind — these are called the venerable.

blocks.text: The obstacles to insight, then the twelfth provision: generosity.

"I was born into a noble family and went forth with genuine faith, not like other monks." Or: "I have great learning." Venerable Miào Jìng: with such pride, the elders won't want to teach you. Master Cháng Bǎi: without a humble wish for the Dharma, one cannot learn.

"Having attained only a small, inferior degree of knowledge and insight, one rests content in it" and becomes conceited. Restlessness scatters the mind. These obstruct insight. Freedom from obstruction is when such obstacles "have never taken root, are absent, do not arise".
"Giving whose nature is blameless, undertaken to adorn the mind, to support the mind, to provide resources for yogic practice, and to attain the highest good."
"Giving with one's own hand is called being a giver. Giving one's own property, willingly, is called being a donor."

items: **Those in hardship**: the poor, beggars, travellers, the blind and deaf, those without refuge.
**Those who have shown kindness**: parents, those who nursed and raised one, who rescued one in hardship. Venerable Miào Jìng reads 引 as "enlarging" one's benefit.
**The venerable**: renunciants acknowledged as virtuous. Master Cháng Bǎi tells how Śāriputra offered food to the Buddha.

quiz.q: One who is conceited cannot respectfully question the elders. What follows, according to the two masters?
options: Miào Jìng: being so proud, the elders are unwilling to teach; Cháng Bǎi: without a humble wish for the Dharma, the elders will not open it to the arrogant
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: with such pride, the elders won't want to teach you. Master Cháng Bǎi: without a wish for the Dharma and humble requests, elder monks of great wisdom will not open the teaching to such proud practitioners.

quiz.q: What is freedom from obstruction, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "does not coincide" and "does not arise"?
options: the obstruction is absent, removed, not coinciding, not arising; avoiding heedlessness and bad places is "not coinciding," avoiding conceit and restlessness "not arising"
quiz.why: "Namely, that this obstruction has never taken root, is absent, does not coincide, and does not arise: this is called freedom from obstruction." Venerable Miào Jìng: being free of heedlessness and unsuitable places is "not coinciding"; being free of conceit and restlessness is "not arising" — not appearing. The English "never taken root" reads differently.

quiz.q: For what four purposes is generosity undertaken, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "adorning the mind"?
options: adorning and supporting the mind, resourcing yoga, attaining the highest good; frequent giving subdues stinginess and purifies the mind — that is adornment
fame, profit, office, life; fine clothes
quiz.why: "Undertaken to adorn the mind, to support the mind, to provide the resources for yogic practice, and to attain the highest good — is called generosity." Venerable Miào Jìng: giving often subdues the stain of stinginess and makes the mind pure — that is "adornment."

quiz.q: How do "giver" and "donor" differ, according to the two masters?
options: the giver acts with their own hand; the donor owns the gift — entrust it to another and one is only the donor
quiz.why: "Giving with one's own hand is called being a giver. Giving one's own property, willingly and not reluctantly, is called being a donor." Master Cháng Bǎi: the giver actually carries out the giving; the donor owns the gift. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you entrust it to someone else, you are the donor, not the giver.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "those without refuge" (無趣者) among those in hardship?
quiz.why: "The poor, beggars, travellers, seekers, the blind, the deaf, those without support, those without refuge …" Venerable Miào Jìng: those "without refuge" are people with no home to return to.

quiz.q: Among those who showed kindness, how does Venerable Miào Jìng read 引 in "those who 引 benefit and ease"?
options: expanding — someone who enlarges your benefit and ease
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 引 means to expand — the person who enlarges your benefit and your ease. The English "guided" reads it differently.

quiz.q: Discussing the venerable as a field of merit, what story does Master Cháng Bǎi tell to show "an inferior field but a superior mind"?
options: Śāriputra offered food to the Buddha, who fed it to a dog and asked whose merit was greater
quiz.why: The text: the venerable are renunciants or brahmins acknowledged by the world as virtuous. Master Cháng Bǎi: Śāriputra offered food to the Buddha; the Buddha fed it to a dog and asked, "Which of us has the greater merit?" — showing merit depends on more than the field.
